learningObjectives: Explain how threads enable concurrent execution in Java.
Distinguish between common thread states and synchronization concepts.
Construct a basic concurrent workflow using ExecutorService and synchronization.

activities.title: Thread Lifecycle
activities.instruction: Explore the major states in the lifecycle of a Java thread.

content.concept: Java defines thread states such as NEW, RUNNABLE, BLOCKED, WAITING, TIMED_WAITING, and TERMINATED. A thread can move between states depending on scheduling, synchronization, waiting, and completion.

activities.title: Concurrency Concept Map
activities.instruction: Explore the role of common Java concurrency tools.

content.concept: Concurrency requires coordination when multiple tasks execute independently or access shared state. Threads perform work, executors manage task execution, synchronization protects critical sections, and concurrent utilities provide safer coordination patterns.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Manages a pool or group of worker threads and executes submitted tasks.
Provides intrinsic locking for synchronized methods or blocks.
Provides explicit locking mechanisms for coordinated access.
Collections designed to support concurrent access with appropriate thread-safety characteristics.

activities.title: ExecutorService Builder
activities.instruction: Build a basic task-execution workflow using an executor.

content.concept: ExecutorService separates task submission from thread management. Tasks can be submitted to an executor, which schedules them on available worker threads. The executor should be shut down when it is no longer needed.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Shared-State Protection
activities.instruction: Choose the appropriate protection strategy for shared mutable data.

content.concept: When multiple threads access shared mutable state, unsynchronized operations can produce race conditions. Synchronization or other concurrency controls can ensure that critical operations occur safely.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Multiple threads update the same counter → protect the critical update
Each thread works only with independent local variables → synchronization is unnecessary for those variables
config.answer: Multiple threads update the same counter → protect the critical update
